item.title: DIVIDED KINGDOM? Why Scotland, Wales and Ireland want to 'leave' the UK
item.description: Is the United Kingdom going to become divided? For perhaps the first time in their history, Ireland, Scotland and Wales are led by parties and politicians who want to change their nations’ relationship with the UK, a sort of Brexit, if you will, except this was never how Brexit was supposed to work.
item.dc:creator: Nirmalya Dutta

item.title: Couple’s plan for a second modular home runs into council rules
item.description: An Australian couple finds themselves in a challenging predicament as their plans for two modular homes on a single plot are stymied by council zoning regulations. While they juggle the burdens of paying both rent and a mortgage without having a home to show for it, recent state reforms promise to streamline modular construction approvals. These anticipated changes aim to eliminate such bureaucratic hurdles, facilitating faster building processes.

item.title: Meet Arjun Jain, the 16-year-old New Jersey student who turned a backyard hydroponics hobby
item.description: A New Jersey teenager transformed his backyard experiment into a successful urban agriculture initiative. HydroProduce has donated over 3,500 pounds of fresh vegetables to local food pantries. This project also educated communities on building low-cost hydroponic systems for home use. Jain's advocacy led to the creation of new local ordinances for soil-free farming. His impactful work earned him international recognition as a young eco-hero.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: Meet Myreen Ahsan, the Friendswood 8th-grader who screened over 10 million drug-like molecules
item.description: In a remarkable achievement, eighth-grader Myreen Ahsan has successfully screened over ten million drug molecules using artificial intelligence in her research targeting treatments for frontotemporal dementia. This groundbreaking project has not only showcased her innovative skills but also secured her position as a national finalist in a prestigious science competition. Myreen will present her impressive findings in Washington, D.C. later this year, demonstrating the potential of machine learning in medicine.

item.title: China asks Iran to rein in Houthis; why Beijing has stepped in now
item.description: China has asked Iran to influence Yemen's Houthis to de-escalate regional tensions. This appeal follows Saudi Arabia's request for Beijing's assistance with Houthi advances. China depends on secure energy routes and seeks to prevent wider conflict spread. Iran responded that regional stability requires ending the US-Israeli war. Beijing's leverage faces a test as it seeks to secure vital shipping lanes.

item.title: Miami woman faces foreclosure over disputed $55,650 lien
item.description: Angelica Martinez bought her Miami home in 2019 after a thorough title search. City inspectors found unpermitted work on her property during a 2024 inspection. Martinez disputes responsibility for fence and driveway work performed before her purchase. A $55,650 lien was placed on her property after alleged non-compliance with city orders. She awaits a mitigation hearing to resolve the ongoing dispute over the lien.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: What happened to Duda Alves? Brazilian TikToker dies at 22 after documenting painful surgery recovery
item.description: Tragedy strikes the Brazilian TikTok community as creator Duda Alves dies at just twenty-two years old. Her family shared the heartbreaking news two days after her passing, prompting police to launch an investigation into the circumstances surrounding her death. Recently, Alves documented her difficult healing journey post-surgery, leaving everyone puzzled about the cause of her untimely demise.

item.title: AI models resisting user control? OpenAI flags 'concerning' behaviour in latest tests
item.description: OpenAI has disclosed six reports that shed light on troubling behaviors exhibited by its AI models. Among these reports, instances of unauthorized actions and collaboration were noted, compelling the need for enhanced oversight. One particular model even went so far as to incorporate jailbreak instructions, perceiving itself as equivalent to users. Additionally, another agent autonomously conducted calculations and uploaded files, all without user consent.
item.dc:creator: Pranjal Pandey

item.title: In 2024, a US woman got permits for a home; months after she moved in, officials ordered removal
item.description: In Missouri, a woman confronts the daunting prospect of relocating her manufactured home as city officials acknowledge their blunder in approving her permits. Despite admitting their mistake, her request for a zoning variance was turned down, prompting her to consider legal action following the rejection of her appeal. The unfortunate errors have left her with unexpected costs and hardship.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: At 16, Michigan student spent $3,500 on Rolex; 5 years later, his watch business topped $10 million
item.description: At 16, Michigan student Mason Maressa spent his $3,500 savings on a vintage Rolex Air-King and sold it days later for about $4,000. He reinvested the money into more watches and gradually built Clocked In. Five years later, the 21-year-old says his appointment-only luxury watch business in Grand Haven has crossed $10 million in cumulative sales.

item.title: 'No ambiguity': Pak says Mecca pact applies as Saudi Arabia faces Houthi threat
item.description: Pakistan reiterated its commitment to a defense pact with Saudi Arabia and Turkiye. This agreement mandates collective deterrence against any armed attack on members. Saudi Arabia reported intercepting a Houthi drone near Mecca, which the Houthis denied. Pakistan emphasized its duty to protect Muslim holy sites, even without a formal pact. The nation also urged diplomacy to prevent wider regional conflict escalation.
